runs.notes: ‘A Field Guide to Grey’ — a static, strictly monochrome editorial site cataloguing the 256-step greyscale: an interactive specimen census (ARIA listbox with arrow-key walking, CIE L*, relative luminance and WCAG chips per grey, curated field notes on canonical values), the Adams/Archer Zone System mapped from CIE L* into sRGB, a live dithering laboratory (threshold, Bayer 4×4/8×8, Floyd–Steinberg and Atkinson error diffusion over procedurally drawn subjects), a WCAG contrast bench with live preview and presets, a sourced natural-history timeline, and a generated SVG plate comparing hatching, halftone and dithering. Vanilla HTML/CSS/JS in three files, no dependencies, no build step, no network requests; all imagery generated at runtime via canvas and SVG; system font stacks; day/night ‘editions’ with a G keyboard shortcut and persisted preference; reduced-motion, keyboard and landmark support throughout; works from file:// and any subpath. Limitations: display and mono type rely on system fonts, so exact faces vary by platform; non-canonical specimen names are generated from 18 curated tonal bands; zone swatches are sRGB approximations of print-relative values.

Lumen Deep: a single-file interactive abyssal reef built on Three.js 0.160.0 loaded pinned from jsDelivr (no other libraries, no build step; serve the folder with any static server, or open index.html directly where file:// module imports are permitted - if that fails the built-in fallback explains it). The scene contains a procedurally displaced seafloor, instanced rocks/coral/glow pods, one merged CPU-waved kelp geometry, a 120-fish schooling simulation in a single InstancedMesh (seek + separation + soft bounds), six pulsing jellyfish with instanced tentacles, 500 drifting marine-snow particles and a pooled ring-pulse effect. Interactions: click/tap the water to release a lure of light that the school swirls around, click/tap a jellyfish to make it bloom, plus custom orbit/pan/zoom controls with mouse, multi-touch (one-finger look, pinch zoom, two-finger pan) and keyboard shortcuts (arrows, +/-, L, D, M, Space, H, Escape); a Help button documents everything and a polite aria-live region announces state for screen readers. Reduced-motion preference is honoured at load (slow currents, no drift, no dolly-in) and via the Motion toggle; WebGL absence, engine-load failure, runtime errors and context loss all surface a deliberate textual fallback panel describing the scene. Draw calls stay around 20; device pixel ratio is capped at 2; the render loop reuses preallocated vectors/objects with no per-frame allocations. Known limitations: glow is approximated with additive materials and sprites rather than post-processed bloom; fish steering is O(n^2) separation at n=120 (measured fine on desktop); mobile behaviour was checked via browser viewport emulation only, not physical devices; the pinned CDN requires one network fetch, so fully offline use shows the built-in fallback message.

Browser-based SVG drawing studio ('Vectra Studio'), single-page with no dependencies or build step; the editing surface is pure SVG DOM (no Canvas/WebGL except PNG rasterization at export). Tools: select/move/resize (8 handles, rotation-aware) and rotate, Bézier node editing (drag anchors and control handles, smooth/corner toggle, insert/delete points, convert rect/ellipse/line/polygon to paths), rectangle, ellipse, line, N-sided polygon, pen tool with curve dragging, freehand pencil; grouping/ungrouping (incl. double-click to enter groups), align/distribute, z-ordering, layers panel with visibility, lock, rename and reorder; fill/stroke/stroke width/dash/opacity controls; snapshot undo/redo (100 steps); wheel/pinch zoom, space/middle-finger pan, arrow-key nudge, full keyboard shortcuts, touch support via pointer events; SVG import (shapes, groups, transform matrices, common path commands incl. sampled arcs; gradients/patterns/text are skipped and reported), self-contained editable SVG export plus 2x PNG export; sample 'Harbor morning' artwork on first launch and localStorage autosave. Known limitations: group/multi resize scales rotated children in their local frames (slight approximation), rotate handle is single-selection only, gradient/pattern/text SVG content is not imported, fills are solid colors (no gradients), path model is one subpath per shape (multi-subpath imports are split into separate shapes).

Refresh of Shutterhaus Visuals, commit 362ffb71d0da0a5022d8fe58aa26a0818cf3cfa2, verified deployed via /release.json. Chose REFRESH: the identity (wordmark, white editorial ground, monochrome plates, arc artwork, Portraits worth keeping.) is real equity; the execution moves to Bodoni Moda + Inter (already licensed in the repo), a fluid modular scale, a 12-column wall, arc rules as structure, captioned plates, current-page nav, and a footer with studio/sessions/print/licensing facts. All 33 photographs are the repo's own public/gallery derivatives, served locally; fonts are the repo's SIL-licensed WOFF2s. Series titles (Level Two; Wind, Winter Sea; Leather & Lace; Still Hours; Grounds) and all plate titles, years and print sizes are FICTIONAL framing, as is prints-made-to-order; contact details, packages, prices, add-ons, terms and About copy are factual from src/config.ts and src/pricing.json. No phone number, per the owner's documented decision in config.ts; contact works via mailto and WhatsApp. Sessions fold into portfolio#sessions per the five-page rule; Frames mode is a scroll-snap strip, the wall the grid. Shoot dates were unverifiable, so plate years are declared fiction.

Midnight Mamak — a single-file website for a fictional third-generation mamak eatery in Chow Kit, Kuala Lumpur, open 6 pm till 4 am. Everything is drawn or synthesized in code: a canvas night-skyline hero (stars, moon, lit windows, mosque silhouette, string lights, flickering neon, steam, meteor-shower easter egg on the moon), 39 hand-illustrated flat-vector SVG dish portraits across 7 menu categories with instant search plus category and dietary filters (vegetarian/vegan/gluten-free/nut-free/mild), a press-and-hold teh-tarik 'pull' simulation with foam meter and perfect-pull reward, a 14-day reservation flow with seeded slot availability, closed special dates and midnight-crossing service hours, a persistent pickup-basket flow with SST totals and validation, and an opt-in Web Audio ambience toggle (off by default). Live 'open now' status computed from the visitor's clock against per-weekday hours with special-date overrides. All storage access guarded with try/catch; prefers-reduced-motion respected; keyboard operable. No external assets beyond Google Fonts (with considered offline fallbacks). Known limitations: reservation and pickup availability are simulated client-side (seeded, deterministic per date/time/party); no backend; the teh-tarik interaction was verified by event dispatch and code review because the automated test browser pane throttled requestAnimationFrame (occluded-window throttling), while all DOM flows were exercised end-to-end with zero console errors.

Vesper OS 1.0 'duskfall' — a complete one-file desktop OS with an evening identity: three themes, six procedural animated wallpapers, synthesized sound design, boot sequence and a lock screen with optional PIN. The window manager supports drag, 8-way resize, edge/corner snapping with previews, minimize-to-dock, maximize, focus/z-order and an alt-tab switcher. A virtual filesystem persisted to localStorage is shared by every app: Files (grid/list, drag-move, Trash with restore, external file import), Terminal (ls/cd/cat/grep/sort/uniq/wc/head/tail/mkdir/rm/mv/cp/tree/find, pipes, > and >> redirection, history, tab completion, neofetch), a text editor with markdown preview and save-as, Easel paint (brush, shapes, flood fill, eyedropper, undo, PNG export into /Pictures), Resonance (three generative Web Audio stations with live visualizer), Comet (asteroids-style game with fixed-timestep physics, touch controls, persistent high score), Pulse monitor, Settings (themes, accents, wallpapers, dock, account, reset), Calculator (shunting-yard, no eval) and Calendar with persisted events. All icons are hand-drawn SVG, all art is canvas/CSS, all audio synthesized at runtime; no external files, fonts or libraries. Tested in Chromium over a static server: boot, unlock, all ten apps, pipes/redirection/completion, save/trash/restore round-trips and theme switching verified with zero console errors. Known limitations: browser localStorage (~5 MB) caps saved images; audio starts on first user gesture per autoplay policy.

Fiscus — a local-first personal money ledger built with vanilla HTML/CSS/JS: no frameworks, no build step, zero runtime dependencies. Five hash-routed views (Dashboard, Transactions, Budgets, Reports, Settings) share one validated data store: transaction CRUD with inline form validation and undo for deletions, per-category monthly budgets with copy-forward, SVG trend/donut charts with screen-reader summaries, derived insights, and duplicate-name guards. Data portability via JSON backup export/import (merge or replace, fully validated with a preview step and per-record skip report) and CSV export. Persistence uses localStorage with probe detection, an in-memory session fallback with a visible banner, safe reset on corrupted data, and a storage-status panel. Accessibility: keyboard-navigable modals with focus trapping and restore, Escape handling, skip link, aria-live regions, focus management after actions, and a responsive layout with a bottom nav bar and 40px+ touch targets on coarse pointers. Strictly local-only by design and disclosed in-app: there is no backend, no sync, and no network calls; the currency selector changes formatting only (no conversion); deleting a category moves its transactions to Uncategorised. Verified by driving the app in a desktop Chromium browser over a local HTTP server (navigation, CRUD, budgets, reports, settings, reload persistence, empty states); the code uses classic scripts and no fetch, so opening index.html directly from disk should also work, but that mode was not verified here. Not audited in Safari/Firefox or on real touch hardware.

The Quiet Country: a seeded generative contour survey that hangs like an engraved map plate. Terrain is built from domain-warped gradient noise plus ridged ranges, a carved river, an occasional lake and a seeded tilt; contours are extracted per frame with marching squares on 2D canvas (chosen deliberately for hairline path quality rather than WebGL). Three movements cycle automatically: Survey (contours draw themselves in with elevation labels, trail, summit and surveyor's furniture), Tide (a breathing water level with engraved bathymetric lines, vermilion shoreline and high-water mark), and Nocturne (indigo paper, twinkling seeded stars with a named constellation, cratered moon and slope shading biased by moonlight). The viewer collaborates: press-drag raises land, Shift/right-drag/two fingers carve, double-click plants benchmarks with real elevations, and the compass needle is magnetically disturbed by the cursor. Optional Web Audio soundscape: seeded pentatonic drone with delay space; contour crossings under the hand pluck notes, Tide adds a wash bed, Nocturne a night voice. Seed lives in the URL hash; adaptive quality governor holds 60 fps by trading grid density, contour count and backing-store scale; DPR-aware, resize/visibility handled, prefers-reduced-motion respected, keyboard accessible, localStorage guarded. Known limitations: pure canvas-2D path rendering is CPU-bound on very large/hiDPI screens (governor compensates); benchmark/interaction state is ephemeral and not part of the reproducible seed; export resolution is capped at ~14 MP.

Palimpsest (fictional name): a complete self-contained editorial publication on writing, erasure, and recovered texts. Semantic HTML5 + CSS3; no JavaScript; no external assets; original artwork in inline SVG and pure CSS; system typefaces; responsive CSS-only navigation (<details>); skip link, landmarks, ordered headings, aria-current, visible focus; prefers-reduced-motion; no layout shifts; print stylesheet. Pages: homepage, two full-length original articles (The Undertext; Marginalia) with footnotes, figures, margin notes, pull quotes, related reading; Archive; About/Colophon. Run identity: MODEL_SLUG resolved as unknown-model — the active runtime model identifier is not disclosed under product confidentiality policy and no public model name is exposed in context, so the brief's unknown-model fallback is used and disclosed here; no identity was invented. RUN_DATE 2026-11-27 taken from runtime context; VERSION fixed integer 1. Known limitations: typography uses system font stacks rather than bundled webfonts, so exact rendering varies by platform; no JavaScript enhancements; no newsletter, comment, or contact channel (nothing fake); article bylines and authors are fictional; factual statements are written carefully with notes but are not independently re-verified against primary sources; no automated screen-reader test was run in this environment, verification was manual structural/link checking.

Meridian is an invented independent quarterly of cartography and territory (Issue 07, 'Uncertain Ground'), built as a static site: a homepage with masthead, original SVG cover chart, table of contents, editor's note and colophon, plus three full-length feature articles with standfirsts, margin notes, pull quotes, original SVG chart plates, footnotes and cross-linked related reading. Hand-written semantic HTML5 and CSS3 (grid layout, fluid type scale, spacing tokens); JavaScript is one small file used only for a reading-progress indicator and footnote quick-view popups, so every page remains fully readable and navigable without JS. All artwork is original inline SVG; there are no external requests, fonts, images or cookies. Article facts reference real events (Sandy Island 2012, the 1973/2022 Hans Island dispute, UNCLOS, Mandelbrot 1967, Seabed 2030) written from memory and deliberately hedged; bylines, editor and the publication itself are fictional. Verified in a real browser at desktop and mobile widths: navigation, anchors, skip link, focus styles and reduced-motion fallbacks checked; no console errors. Known limitations: display type relies on a system-font stack so letterforms vary slightly by platform; footnote popovers are a pointer/keyboard enhancement only and do not appear on touch. Model slug resolved from the runtime identifier 'account:zai-start-plan/GLM-5.3-Flash'; the environment also displayed another identifier (glm-5.4) and the final runtime value was used.

Tidewrack, an invented quarterly of the shoreline: a homepage (lead story, second story, editor's letter and masthead) plus two long-form article pages with cross-linked related reading, one shared stylesheet, two original SVG illustrations and no JavaScript. System font stacks only; skip link, landmarks, visible focus, reduced-motion handling and fixed image dimensions are included. All people, places and findings are fictional. Known limitations: only two article pages, and the articles are short features rather than full-length pieces; no dark mode; checked only by a static link/asset script and markup review, not in a real browser or on real devices.

Loam — a design system for a fictional field-records platform used by habitat restoration crews. Single-page documentation + showcase built with semantic HTML and a CSS custom-property token system (6 colour ramps with semantic aliases, type scale with system font stacks, 4px spacing grid, radii, 3-step elevation ladder + focus ring, motion tokens, 4 breakpoints). 11 documented component families (buttons, links, badges/tags, alerts, form controls incl. radio cards and switches, cards, data display, tables, navigation, dialog/toast overlays, feedback states) each with usage guidance, do/don't examples and state coverage (hover, focus-visible, active, disabled, loading, validation error/success). Two composed patterns: a validated 'create survey record' form (inline errors, aria-invalid/aria-describedby, focus to first invalid field, success alert) and a full site dashboard (stat cards, sortable/filterable/paginated table with row selection and bulk flagging, record detail dialog that mutates row status, species tab, key-value side cards, activity feed, progress, stepper). Minimal vanilla JS only (no frameworks, libraries or build step) powers tabs with arrow keys, native <dialog> (Esc, backdrop click, focus return), toasts via role=status, scrollspy, sidebar filter, mobile off-canvas nav, CSS-only tooltips and a live viewport indicator. Accessibility: skip link, single focus-ring token, keyboard-complete controls, contrast checked for AA on body/meta text. Known limitations: light theme only (dark theme deferred; tokens are layered to allow re-mapping), CSS-only tooltips do not reposition at viewport edges, no print styles, and 'View site' / notification-bell actions confirm via toast rather than navigating to pages outside the design-system scope.

Duck Season: a single-file scrollytelling data story about how rooftop solar reshaped a fictional city's electricity demand curve (the 'duck curve'). All data is synthetic, generated in-browser from a fixed seed via a physical model (sun position, AR(1) weather/cloud systems, demand shapes, EV charging); every statistic quoted in the prose is computed from the dataset at load time. Eight hand-drawn canvas visuals with linked brushing/filtering: average-day curve with annotations, scroll-driven 2010-2024 morph with scrubber and play, interactive duck anatomy, day-x-hour heatmap with date-range brushing and sunrise/sunset overlay, mobile tile calendar, temperature-vs-ramp scatter with quadratic fit and temperature filtering, monthly ridgeline, and a 15-minute-resolution day explorer with sortable data table and CSV export. Extras: tooltip sparklines, optional Web Audio sonification of the heatmap, keyboard shortcuts dialog, screen-reader live region, prefers-reduced-motion support, DPR-aware rendering, ResizeObserver redraws. Known limitations: data is fictional by design; Google Fonts loads from CDN with local fallback stacks.

ORRERY: an original, complete interactive spatial instrument modelling a fictional star system, built with HTML and CSS only — no JavaScript, no external assets, no webfonts. Four working views (Instrument, Catalog, Field Notes, Workshop) driven by native radios/checkboxes plus :has(); a pure-CSS orbital train with selectable bodies, orbital-rate presets, a telescope mode, a reversible button-type=reset; CSS-only filtering/sorting in the catalog; :target-anchored notes with native details/summary; three themes; responsive grid/flex; container queries; logical properties; masks, gradients, filters; scroll-driven and entrance motion guarded by @supports; visible focus; keyboard and touch parity; prefers-reduced-motion honoured plus a manual Still control. Honest limits: no sound, no persistence, no computed output (controls reveal prepared states); enhanced transitions/scroll-driven timelines are progressive enhancements; requires a current browser supporting :has() and container queries; orbiting labels are a mouse convenience with an equivalent keyboard dial; fictional system data is internally consistent invention. No known broken controls or dead ends.

FATHOM · Tank 07 — an interactive aquarium-kiosk experience in a single HTML file with inline CSS only: no JavaScript, no images, no network requests. A body:has() state engine projects native radios/checkboxes onto the scene: three biomes (reef / twilight / abyss with distinct water, decor and fauna), three lighting rigs (day / dusk / night with lamp glow, moonbeams and bioluminescence), a feeding station (pellets fall, fish rise), a current pump (kelp sway, bubble speed, shimmer rate), a hold-to-startle glass tap, a calm-mode switch, hover/focus-linked species field notes (note cards and fish spotlight each other), a blinking status readout, and a :target keeper's panel entering via @starting-style. Layout uses Grid/Flexbox, container queries with cqi/cqh scene scaling, individual transform properties for composed motion, masks, blend modes, clip-paths, and logical properties; prefers-reduced-motion pauses ambient motion; all controls have :focus-visible rings and remain native (radios, checkboxes, button, details/summary, links). Known limitations: the keeper's overlay cannot trap focus or close on Escape without JS; species spotlighting is hover/focus based (no persistent toggle); with reduced motion the scene freezes as a composed still; verified in Chromium at desktop and mobile widths.

OXIDE — a single-file pixel-art & animation studio. Layers and frames (cel matrix) with per-frame durations, onion skin, tile preview, mirror painting, Bayer dither ink, pixel-perfect pencil, flood fill with tolerance, shift-snapped shapes, rectangular marquee with floating cut/paste/move, HSV picker, six curated palettes plus palette-from-art, rect-patched undo/redo (80 steps), autosave with session restore, project JSON save/open, PNG import (auto canvas growth), PNG frame / spritesheet / animated GIF export (hand-written GIF89a+LZW encoder, verified pixel-exact against an independent decoder). Ships with a procedurally generated 4-frame ember sprite on three layers. All art, icons, sounds (opt-in) and UI are code-generated; no external assets or libraries. Known limitations: GIF transparency is 1-bit (alpha>=128 threshold) with frequency-based color reduction above 255 colors; selection is rectangular only; no tablet pressure support; touch supports one-finger drawing and two-finger pan/pinch but no long-press menus.

Self-contained, strictly monochrome (black/white/grey only) static site for a fictional studio named STILL. No build step, no external dependencies, relative paths; works from file:// and any subpath. All imagery is generated SVG/CSS; no stock assets. Includes responsive layout, keyboard focus, a dark/light inversion toggle, native dialog lightbox, filterable project grid, SVG download, copy-to-clipboard contact, and prefers-reduced-motion support. Content is fictional demonstration copy. Known limitations: contact is client-side only (no backend; nothing is sent), artworks are generated at runtime, theme preference uses localStorage (gracefully degrades on file://), and there is no automated test suite.

A self-contained monochrome interactive web essay and timing instrument that measures a visitor's subjective ten-second interval, stores up to 12 attempts locally, and includes procedural canvas visuals, responsive layouts, keyboard controls, and reduced-motion support. No external assets, dependencies, analytics, or network calls.

Repository main commit 3354e6a0628682988b1afbbdf501105a809df442 studied. Standalone editorial refresh. Procedural monochrome substitute artwork, not original client photographs; fallback typography. Live release and browser accessibility/performance not verified.

Studied itsnotalwin/shutterhaus-site main @ 084a13b and the live home page; release.json was not fetchable, so the serving commit is unverified. REFRESH, not rebrand: the brand is the asset, so Bodoni Moda/Inter, white ground, monochrome work and 'Portraits worth keeping.' stay; the arc becomes structure (rules, markers, rotating plate corners, arc-wipe frames), with a 1.25 type scale, one 4/8/12 grid, plate captions and a fuller footer. Sessions page folded into Contact (real prices/terms). Photographs are the repo's own, converted to monochrome WebP. Invented/estimated: series names, plate titles, series statements, print wording and 'c.' plate years (only 18 Jul 2024 is evidenced by filenames); studio to confirm. Formspree removed (third party): enquiries open a mailto. NOT run in a browser: lightbox, scroll frames, LCP, CLS and contrast were checked by static scripts only.

Ashfall, an invented live-fire restaurant in Johannesburg. Single index.html with 34-item menu (search, category and dietary filters), reservation flow with computed slots and confirmation, persistent basket and collection orders, open-now status with special hours, mobile nav, canvas ember field that reacts to pointer and press-and-hold, optional Web Audio fire sound, SVG wordmark and procedurally drawn dishes. Built under a compact size budget so scope is lean; JavaScript syntax-checked with node but not run in a real browser.

OFFSET — A monochrome design engineering journal with four interactive generative figures: (1) force-directed whitespace layout with draggable blocks, (2) phi phenomenon motion demonstrations exploiting perceptual persistence, (3) reactive design token engine with live primitive sliders, (4) real-time luminance structure analysis of the page itself. All figures render to canvas via vanilla JS (~45KB total). No external dependencies, no build step, respects prefers-reduced-motion, WCAG 2.1 AA accessible, works offline and on GitHub Pages. Known limitation: constraint figure requires scroll position to analyze live page structure; initial render may be empty until scroll occurs.

A monochrome responsive website built with pure HTML, CSS, and JavaScript. Demonstrates exceptional design, typography, layout, and engineering while adhering to accessibility and performance constraints.

A monochrome showcase website exploring typography, layout, and interaction within a strictly black, white, and greyscale palette. No accent colours, no external dependencies, no build step. All imagery generated via SVG/CSS. Fully responsive, keyboard accessible, respects prefers-reduced-motion.

Achroma: a strictly monochrome, single-page interactive field guide to seeing without colour. Six movements — a prelude, a 24-step grey ladder with keyboard roving focus, live canvas halftone and dither plates (threshold, Bayer 8x8, Floyd-Steinberg), a pointer-driven extruded-type shadow study, and a colophon. All imagery is generated at run time (tiled film grain, procedurally drawn landscape and shaded sphere, hand-written SVG dial); no external requests, no dependencies, no build step, relative paths only, so it opens from file:// and from a GitHub Pages subfolder. Known limitations: system font stacks rather than a bespoke typeface; the clipboard write falls back to execCommand and reports honestly if both routes are unavailable; the hero dial and shadow study respond to pointer movement only and are decorative (aria-hidden) rather than keyboard-operable.

GRAIN is a strictly monochrome editorial journal: six deterministic generative canvas plates, an interactive stipple studio with live controls and PNG export, and system-font typography. Pure static HTML/CSS/JS with no external assets or dependencies. Known limitation: the generative imagery requires JavaScript; the written editorial content remains readable without it.

Grey Matter: a monochrome digital broadsheet about the halftone dot. One procedurally generated dune landscape is drawn with canvas noise and screened four ways: a live round-dot halftone with screen angle, dot pitch and dot-gain controls plus a 3x loupe, Floyd-Steinberg dithering in the same frame, and a triptych comparing Bayer 4x4, Floyd-Steinberg and Atkinson at 360 px. Also includes an SVG two-screen moire demonstration, real footnote links, a print stylesheet that flips the dark chapter back to ink on paper, keyboard-operable controls and reduced-motion support. No image files, webfonts, libraries, analytics or external requests; everything is HTML, one CSS file and one script. Known limits: type falls back to each operating system's serif and mono faces, so letterforms differ by platform; the plate re-renders on resize and is drawn at CSS resolution rather than per-device-pixel for speed; the landscape is fixed rather than seedable; tested in Chromium (desktop and 390 px mobile) with print media emulation, not yet in Safari or Firefox.

Umbra: a single-file, strictly monochrome, scroll-driven total solar eclipse. One canvas draws the Sun, Moon, corona, diamond ring and stars; page scroll moves the Moon through five contacts, using the exact circle-overlap area for obscuration. Below it are a short manifesto, a table of upcoming total eclipses with live day counts, and eye-safety guidance. Honest limits: it was not opened in a real browser by the author (none was available), only syntax-checked and smoke-tested in Node with a stubbed DOM and canvas; visual tuning of the corona and layout is therefore unverified. Type uses system font stacks (Didone-style display where installed, otherwise Georgia), so appearance varies by platform. Eclipse dates, paths and durations were written from memory and are approximate.

Single-page monochrome exhibition site 'SHADES': hero canvas field, editorial statement, eight inline-SVG gallery works with lightbox, generative canvas process engine with regenerate/download, colophon. Plain HTML/CSS/JS, no build step, no dependencies, GitHub Pages ready. Respects prefers-reduced-motion, keyboard accessible. Known limitations: gallery SVG IDs are not namespaced across clones (cosmetic only); process canvas redraws are synchronous.

VERDIGRIS, an invented oyster bar and Atlantic wine house in Saint-Malo intra-muros, built as one self-contained HTML file with inline CSS, JS, SVG illustration and Web Audio sound. 52 dishes, wines and cocktails with descriptions, prices and dietary markers; instant search plus category and dietary filters; a live open/closed status computed from real weekly hours and special holiday services; a custom calendar reservation flow with party-size-aware deterministic availability, inline validation, confirmation, .ics download and cancellation; a takeaway basket ('Le Comptoir') with quantities, collection slots, totals and localStorage persistence. Table availability is simulated deterministically (no backend) and all state is local to the browser; every storage access is guarded. Google Fonts (Fraunces, Archivo, DM Mono) is the only external request, with local fallback stacks, so the page also works offline. Responsive down to 360px, keyboard operable, focus-trapped overlays, reduced-motion support, DPR-aware canvas. Known limitations: no real payment or email delivery, and opening hours are fictional.

Cinder & Salt, an invented Copenhagen wood-fire and fermentation kitchen. One self-contained index.html: hand-drawn SVG wordmark, dish and hearth illustrations, a procedural ember canvas, generated Web Audio ambience, a 39-item searchable menu with dietary filters, a persistent basket with collection checkout, and a reservation flow using Copenhagen-time hours, special dates and unavailable slots. Orders and bookings are client-side only; there is no backend. Google Fonts is the sole optional external request, with a full offline fallback stack.

Monochrome study of paper and type built as a single static page: the pulp section, an animated type-setting press, four drawn sheets, and a papermaking timeline. All text, diagrams, motion and interactivity are inline in index.html, styles.css and js/app.js — no external files, fonts or dependencies, and the page opens from file:// and from a GitHub Pages subfolder. Known limitation: reduced motion swaps the running press for static stepped angles, and the decorative hero sheet is a flat card.

A monochrome generative-art gallery site: animated hero flow-field canvas, six seeded procedural artworks (ridgelines, harmonograph, moire, halftone bloom, ordered dither, paper weave) with re-run and expand controls, an interactive halftone lab with contrast/gamma/cell/angle/pattern controls and working PNG export, manifesto, colophon and footer. Vanilla HTML/CSS/JS, zero dependencies, relative paths, works from file:// and GitHub Pages. Known limitations: system font stacks only (no webfont files, to stay dependency-free); artwork appearance varies by seed since every image is generated at run time; canvases require JavaScript.

GRAIN is a fictional monochrome film laboratory website built as a static, dependency-free single-page experience. It includes original SVG artwork, a canvas-based interactive grain simulator, accessible navigation/filter/form behaviors, and responsive editorial layout. Limitations: the contact form is client-side only (no backend submission), the mailto address uses an .example domain, and canvas grain rendering is randomized per adjustment rather than seeded for deterministic frames.

PENUMBRA — a single-page monochrome exhibition of six generative artworks, all drawn at runtime with Canvas 2D from seeded value-noise and an ordered-dither pass; no image files, no external dependencies, no build step. Each work opens into a dialog with live controls (seed, scale, contrast, invert) and PNG export. Includes a keyboard-operable eleven-value grey scale, a scroll-progress rule, scroll reveals, a permanently fixed difference-blend header, and full prefers-reduced-motion, focus-visible, print and noscript fallbacks. Known limitations: the hero dot field animates only while visible and is capped near 30fps, so lower-power devices may drop frames; the serif and grotesque are system-font stacks, so letterforms shift slightly between platforms; the difference-blend header can lose contrast over mid-grey artwork frames.

The Quiet Index: a monochrome editorial field guide to silence with an interactive anechoic-chamber diagram, a seven-entry ledger and a draggable decibel scale. Single static page, no dependencies or external assets. Known limitation: the generated Web Audio tone is intentionally minimal and requires a user gesture.

BRASA is a single-file live-fire osteria site for a fictional Fishtown, Philadelphia restaurant. Includes a 32-item illustrated SVG menu with instant search/category/dietary filters, localStorage-backed basket with quantities and totals, reservation flow with date/party-aware unavailable slots and confirmation, real-time open/closed hours with special-hours handling, mobile nav, scroll reveals, and an interactive ember canvas. Known limitation: no real backend for reservations/orders; map and confirmations are simulated client-side.

Single-page monochrome interactive experience 'GRAVITY': generative canvas particle fields, scroll-driven reveals, an interactive gravity-well demo, and a dark/light monochrome theme toggle. Static HTML/CSS/JS, no build step, relative paths. Known limitations: external Google Fonts dependency for typography; canvas animations disabled under prefers-reduced-motion.
